correctness.rationale: For each n in a single Fibonacci interval, the summand count equals one plus the translated count, so induction reduces n. All intervals crossing a Fibonacci boundary lie among four explicitly tabulated offsets, with formulas proved by a two-step Fibonacci-index recurrence from F9 and F10. For d=2,3 two boundary parities differ; for d=1,4 two adjacent counts are equal. The equal odd divisors of two adjacent odd integers must equal one; all eligible odd Fibonacci pairs are (1,3),(3,5), leaving the sole triple (1,3,5). Greedy checks and symbolic boundary cases were rechecked from packaged VERIFY.py; finite checks are not the infinite proof.

originality.rationale: Exact statement/implication comparison with the accessible complete motivating paper finds neither the odd three-term progression classification nor the step-two parity-rigidity lemma. The cited paper only forces restrictions on longer step-two runs and on equal digit counts along Fibonacci steps; neither entails this universal three-point parity statement. Targeted published-finding corpus and web searches found no equivalent. The indexed but uninspected companion manuscript and broader Fibonacci-automatic literature remain genuine residual risks.
